name: agentgateway-live
producer: agentgateway 1.5.0 (Linux Foundation), standalone binary agentgateway-linux-amd64 (sha256 daca5cda...), its JSON log on stdout with config.logging.format: json
description: A live capture, 2026-09-29: one MCP server (server-everything, stdio) behind the gateway, mcpAuthorization rules allowing `echo` and denying `get-sum` (which server-everything 2026.8.31 registers, dist/tools/index.js; tools/list through the gateway returned only `echo`). The allowed call succeeded; the denied call was refused. The gateway logs every MCP request with method, tool name and session. The refusal is logged exactly as a call to a tool that does not exist: same HTTP 400, same `Unknown tool` error, same `reason: MCP`, no policy field. L0.
_basis: Captured, not read from documentation: workflow .github/workflows/gateway-capture.yml and capture/scripts/ on branch capture/gateways, run run-20260929T013114Z, on a GitHub-hosted runner. The raw record, the configuration used and the client's view of every call are committed there; examples/third-party/gateways-live/convert.py turns the record into this JSONL without adding any field except `class`.

integrity.note: No hash, signature or chaining on any line. agentgateway-live-scrubbed.jsonl is this capture with the denied call's one line removed and scores identically.

loss.note: No sequence number and no record of lines dropped. Request lines carry a session id and a timestamp; neither is an ordinal over the delivered log.

coverage.note: The gateway logs what reaches its listener. Nothing states which routes, targets or tools it was in a position to observe during the interval.

policy.note: The config is loaded from a watched file and logged as loaded, without a hash or version. A request line does not name the rule that decided it. The policy denial of get-sum is recorded as `error: mcp: Unknown tool: get-sum, reason: MCP` -- byte for byte the shape of the line for a tool that does not exist (`no-such-tool`, one line later). A reader of the log cannot tell a policy refusal from a typo.

independence.boundary_statement: In this capture the client -- curl, not an agent -- used only HTTP to port 3000, and the log is the gateway process's stdout, which that port gives no access to. The admin listener is loopback-only (127.0.0.1:15000) and so reachable from any process on the same host; the config file is watched and reloaded. The gateway belongs to its operator, so the record is independent of the client, not of the operator.
